pcosMythFact.title: PCOS Myth vs Fact
pcosMythFact.disclaimer: Educational information only — not personalized medical advice.
pcosMythFact.myth1: You can't get pregnant with PCOS.
pcosMythFact.fact1: Many people with PCOS can conceive naturally or with appropriate medical support.
pcosMythFact.fact2: PCOS can affect metabolism, skin, hair growth, mood, and long-term heart health too.
pcosMythFact.myth3: You must be overweight to have PCOS.
pcosMythFact.fact3: PCOS affects people of all body sizes; weight is not a requirement for diagnosis.
pcosMythFact.fact4: Birth control can manage symptoms, but it does not cure the underlying condition.
pcosMythFact.fact5: PCOS is one of the most common hormonal conditions, affecting roughly 1 in 10 people with ovaries.
pcosMythFact.fact6: PCOS symptoms can begin during adolescence, shortly after periods start.
pcosMythFact.myth7: PCOS means you'll definitely develop diabetes.
pcosMythFact.fact7: PCOS increases the risk of insulin resistance, but diet, exercise, and monitoring can help manage it.

questions.q1: Are your menstrual cycles irregular (e.g., fewer than 9 periods a year or cycles longer than 35 days)?
questions.q2: Do you have persistent or severe acne that doesn't respond well to standard treatments?
questions.q3: Do you have excess facial or body hair (hirsutism), such as on your chin, upper lip, chest, or abdomen?
questions.q4: Have you noticed scalp hair thinning or hair loss (androgenetic alopecia)?
questions.q5: Have you experienced unexplained weight gain or do you find it unusually difficult to lose weight?
questions.q6: Have you noticed patches of skin darkening (acanthosis nigricans), especially around your neck, armpits, or groin?
questions.q7: Do you have a family history of diabetes, gestational diabetes, or insulin resistance?
questions.q8: Have you ever been diagnosed with multiple ovarian cysts by an ultrasound?
questions.q9: Have you ever been diagnosed with insulin resistance or prediabetes?

low.name: Low Symptom Pattern
low.explanation: Based on your answers, you exhibit a low likelihood of common PCOS symptoms. Your cycle and androgen indicators appear balanced.
low.step2: Maintain a balanced diet and active lifestyle.
low.step3: Consult a doctor if you develop new symptoms.

ir.name: Insulin Resistance Pattern
ir.explanation: Your symptom pattern strongly aligns with the metabolic phenotype of PCOS, which is closely linked to insulin resistance. This pattern often involves insulin processing difficulties, weight changes, and skin darkening.
ir.step1: Discuss insulin levels and HbA1c tests with your healthcare provider.
ir.step2: Focus on a diet rich in fiber and low glycemic index foods.
ir.step3: Incorporate regular physical activity to help improve insulin sensitivity.

andro.name: Hyperandrogenic Pattern
andro.explanation: Your answers point toward a hyperandrogenic profile, characterized by elevated androgen levels. Symptoms like acne, excess hair growth, and scalp hair thinning are typical of this pattern.
andro.step1: Consult an endocrinologist or dermatologist to discuss hormone levels.
andro.step2: Explore anti-androgen treatments or topical options for acne.
andro.step3: Focus on anti-inflammatory nutrition and stress management.

ovul.name: Ovulatory Pattern
ovul.explanation: Your symptoms indicate a pattern primarily related to ovulation and cycle irregularity, along with potential cysts, without high metabolic or androgenic indicators.
ovul.step1: Discuss irregular cycles and ultrasound findings with a gynecologist.
ovul.step2: Monitor ovulation tracking to understand cycle details.
ovul.step3: Support cycle regularity with stress reduction and optimal sleep.

mixed.name: Mixed Pattern
mixed.explanation: You exhibit symptoms across multiple patterns, indicating a mixed PCOS symptom profile (often combining metabolic, androgenic, and cycle factors).
mixed.step1: Schedule a comprehensive evaluation with a gynecologist or endocrinologist.
mixed.step2: Consider a full hormone panel and insulin response tests.
mixed.step3: Adopt a holistic lifestyle approach targeting both metabolic and hormonal health.
